opening.argument: The video is framed as a discussion and entertainment piece built around Reddit anecdotes about disturbing material encountered while working on computers. Its title identifies the subject as Reddit stories from computer technicians, and the narration introduces a question-and-story format about experiences with other people's computers. The conditional calorie claim and request to subscribe function as audience engagement and ordinary channel interaction. Nothing connects those prompts to payment, credential collection, an external destination, or a demonstrated transaction, so they do not change the video's primary purpose or establish deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: Computer Techs, What Disturbing Things Did You Find On Computers? (Reddit Stories r/AskReddit)
Redditors who have had to work with other people's computers. What is the most disturbing thing you have found?
If you are new to the channel, you can subscribe. I publish new videos every day.
